# Test fixtures

`triage/` and `sections/` are both fixture **roots**, and nothing documenting a fixture may
live inside either subtree: every `.md` file under an entry store is an entry, so a README
beside `soloed-track.md` is discovered and rejected as one. That is why this file sits
here, one level above both, and describes all of them.

## `sections/` — slices of a real index

Cut once from a locally built view by `tools/extract_section_fixtures.py` and committed,
exactly as `manual-corpus` commits its extraction snapshots. Pointer resolution and the
term check therefore run in CI with `manuals/` absent, with no PDF opened and no embedding
model loaded. Each file carries `schema`, `captured_from` and an `asserts` line saying what
it is for.

Refresh them by rebuilding the corpus and re-running the extractor against the new view;
they are not generated by any test run, and `make test` never invokes it.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `live_sections.json` | the 22 Ableton Live sections the starter set (7.2–7.6) points at, including §18.1.1, which prints `0 dB` and is what 7.3's gain-stage cause depends on |
| `scarlett_sections.json` | the Scarlett's Direct Monitor sections — 7.4's direct-monitoring cause, in the manual that closed the last corpus gap |
| `apc_sections.json` | the APC guide's regions, every one of them unnumbered, so the title form has somewhere to resolve where no section number exists |
| `alesis_sections.json` | the Nitro Max's MIDI Settings and pad note numbers — 7.5's General MIDI and channel causes, which the drum module documents and no other manual does |
| `split_section.json` | §28.24 Limiter, which the chunker packs into three passages: a pointer resolves to all three, in section order, and the term check sees their concatenation |
| `drift/before.json`, `drift/after.json` | §18.6 as extracted, and the same section after a revision renumbered it to §18.7 and edited its text — see `triage/drift/` below |

## `triage/` — entry stores

| Path | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `three_causes_last_demoted.md` | an entry of three causes whose last loses both its check and its fix parses as two causes plus a note, emitting `closing-statement-inferred` naming the demoted section rather than dropping it |
| `drift/` | reject versus flag, with the ledger as the memory |
| `overlapping_scopes/` | 1.9 over intersecting scopes, not identical ones |

### `drift/`

The pointer `ableton/live-12 §18.6` resolves against `sections/drift/before.json` and does
not against `after.json`, with the source still present — 8.4's case, not the removal case.

`soloed-track.md` holds two causes on purpose. Only the first points at the drifting
section, so a flag has to land on that cause and leave the second backed; a fixture with
one cause cannot tell "flagged the right cause" from "flagged the entry".

Neither ledger is named `.pointer-ledger.jsonl`, so the store as committed is the
**first-run** case: no ledger row anywhere, and `after` therefore rejects with
`pointer-unresolved` (2.2). A test copies the one it wants into a temporary store under the
real name:

| File | Copied in as `.pointer-ledger.jsonl` gives |
|---|---|
| `seeded.pointer-ledger.jsonl` | the flag case — §18.6 has a row, so `after` flags the first cause and sets `unbacked` on its passages (8.4, 8.5) rather than rejecting; running against `before` again clears it |
| `corrupt.pointer-ledger.jsonl` | a failure, not a rejection — the second row is truncated mid-string, and the run exits non-zero naming the file and the line |

`entry_keys` is `[]` in both. It is an annotation for the coverage report and no part of
the ledger key, so seeding it would mean minting an entry identity here — which task 13
owns, and which no fixture may fabricate.

### `overlapping_scopes/`

Two entries declaring the same symptom, `A pad triggers the wrong sound`, scoped
`[ableton/live-12]` and `[ableton/live-12, akai/apc-key-25]`. **Both** are rejected and the
duplication reported (1.9).

The scopes are not equal, which is the whole point of the fixture. A duplicate check that
compares device sets for equality passes on this pair and ships two entries that both
answer a Live question — the second is reachable from every session the first is, because
its scope contains the first's. Rejecting only the wider one is wrong too: nothing here
says which the author meant to keep, and 1.9 reports rather than picks.

The causes differ between the two files on purpose. Identical bodies would let a
content-hash duplicate check pass the test without ever comparing symptom against scope.
